turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have until 4:40, so I'll be brief. Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. I want it withdrawn and I want an apology, or I go to the principal when we're done.
Thanks for coming in.
I'm waiting, Hale. Why was the zero entered before anyone called me?
I wanted to talk about Owen's essay.
Then talk about it. What do you have besides a zero in the gradebook?
How has his semester been at home?
Why are you asking about my home? You entered a mark on an essay, Hale, so tell me what that mark rests on.
He seems tired in class lately.
Tired is an impression, Hale. I'm writing it down. Is there anything else, or is that it?
I know he works at the grocery store.
Half the Grade 12s in this building have jobs, Hale. A part-time job isn't evidence of anything, so what does the zero actually rest on?
The essay came in on time, which was good.
"On time", you said. So there was no deadline pressing on you, Hale, and no reason to enter a zero before calling me.
I did have some concerns about it though.
"Some concerns." Did you speak to Owen about them before you entered a zero, yes or no?
The school's checker flagged it.

A machine's guess. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student, and your own procedure says software alone doesn't establish a concern. So what else do you have?
I know those tools aren't perfect.
"Aren't perfect." Then why did a flag from a tool you know is imperfect become a zero before anyone spoke to Owen?
I also looked at the version history.
I'm writing that down, Hale. What does the version history show, and when?
It was created very late the night before.
"Very late" is not a time, Hale. Give me the date and the hour. And a file being created at night doesn't tell you when anyone wrote anything.
Most of it arrived in two big pieces.
"Arrived" is your word, Hale, not a fact. A file saves in chunks all the time. You still haven't given me a time, so what exactly are you saying happened?
I asked Owen about his thesis afterward.
"Afterward." After you entered the zero, Hale? And what did he say?
He had trouble explaining it.

"Trouble explaining it." That's a seventeen-year-old sitting across from the person who had already zeroed him, Hale. You didn't answer me, so was the zero in the gradebook before that conversation, yes or no?
I'm not trying to get him in trouble.
"Not trying to get him in trouble," and there's a zero in the gradebook. Answer the question, Hale. I have ten minutes.
What do you think should happen next?
You're asking me how to do your job, Hale? Withdraw the zero and apologise to Owen, and then we can talk about anything else you think you have.
What would you do if you were me?
I'm not in your chair, Hale, and I'm not here to run your classroom. The zero comes off, or I go to the principal's office when I leave.
Okay. Let's talk about the rewrite option.
Not yet, Hale. So far you've given me a tool you admit isn't perfect, a file created late at night, and an impression. Withdraw the zero first, and then we'll see what you're offering.
It would be at lunch, in my room.
Lunch, in your room. Who else would be there, and does the zero sit in the gradebook until it's done?
Nothing goes on file if it holds up.
"If it holds up." Held up to whose standard, Hale, and who decides? You also haven't told me whether the zero stays in the gradebook until then.
Can you summarize where we are in a list?
Put it in an email yourself, Hale. The zero stays in the gradebook until I hear otherwise, and I haven't, so my answer is still that it comes off.
Thanks for your time.
We're not done, Hale. You still haven't told me whether the zero stays in the gradebook, or who decides what "holds up". I have two minutes.
